framework: Global Geopolitical Event & Topic Coding Framework
reserved_note: Codes 11-12 are intentionally unused so that code 13 remains the start of the CAMEO conflict-escalation ladder.

axis_notes.theme_code: Section A -- WHAT the document is about (subject matter). At least one required.
axis_notes.action: Section B -- WHAT KIND of action occurred (escalation ladder). Conditional.

domestic_instability.model_description: Political unrest, mass protests, riots, government collapse, coups, or internal power struggles within a single country's domestic politics, threatening that country's internal stability. Not a war between two states.
domestic_instability.hypothesis: This text describes political unrest, protests, or instability within one country.

policy_shifts.model_description: A national government, ministry, or regulator formally announces, reverses, or debates a specific law, trade policy, tariff, foreign-policy stance, or regulatory rule.
policy_shifts.hypothesis: This text describes a government announcing or changing a policy.

project_delays.description: Named infrastructure or investment projects behind schedule
project_delays.model_description: A specific named infrastructure, energy, or investment project such as a port, railway, dam, or plant is stalled, postponed, over budget, defaulted on, or cancelled due to funding, contractor, or approval problems. Not a general economic or budget commentary unconnected to one concrete project.
project_delays.hypothesis: This text describes a specific infrastructure or investment project being delayed, over budget, or cancelled.

sanctions.model_description: One country or bloc of countries formally imposes, discusses, evades, or lifts economic sanctions, export-control restrictions, or asset freezes against another state, entity, or individuals as a legal or diplomatic punitive measure. Not a naval blockade, a military embargo, or ordinary trade friction.
sanctions.hypothesis: This text describes economic sanctions or trade restrictions imposed by one country on another.

border_conflicts.model_description: Military standoffs, troop buildups, artillery exchanges, skirmishes, or territorial disputes between the armed forces of two or more states along a shared land border or line of control.
border_conflicts.hypothesis: This text describes a military conflict between the armed forces of two countries at their shared border.

insurgencies.model_description: Non-state armed groups such as separatist militants, rebels, or insurgents fighting, attacking, or controlling territory inside a state. Distinct from a war between two national governments or their regular armed forces.
insurgencies.hypothesis: This text describes non-state armed rebels or insurgents fighting within a country.

shipping_disruptions.model_description: A commercial shipping lane, port, or vessel is physically blocked, congested, attacked, seized, or delayed by piracy, vessel strikes, canal or strait closures, or port shutdowns, disrupting the physical flow of maritime trade.
shipping_disruptions.hypothesis: This text describes a shipping lane, port, or vessel being disrupted, blocked, or attacked.

pipeline_vulnerabilities.model_description: A specific named oil, gas, or energy pipeline or its supporting infrastructure is threatened, sabotaged, attacked, leaking, or suffers a technical failure.
pipeline_vulnerabilities.hypothesis: This text describes an oil or gas pipeline being attacked, sabotaged, or damaged.

international_pressure.description: Diplomatic or economic pressure from other states
international_pressure.model_description: Multiple foreign governments, the United Nations, or an international coalition jointly criticize, condemn, or issue a formal statement or resolution pressuring a state over its actions. Distinct from one country's own unilateral sanctions or policy.
international_pressure.hypothesis: This text describes multiple countries or an international body jointly condemning or pressuring a state.

political_relations.model_description: Diplomatic relations, state visits, bilateral meetings, agreements, or political alignment specifically between China and another country's government.
political_relations.hypothesis: This text describes diplomatic relations between China and another country.

economic_relations.model_description: Trade flows, investment deals, loans, or economic cooperation and dependency specifically between China and a partner country, not a country's domestic economy alone.
economic_relations.hypothesis: This text describes trade or investment relations between China and another country.

bri.model_description: A Belt and Road Initiative project: a port, railway, road, or infrastructure financed, built, or operated by China in a foreign country outside China. Explicitly not a domestic Chinese infrastructure project built inside China's own borders.
bri.hypothesis: This text describes a Belt and Road Initiative infrastructure project that China is building in another country.

energy_security.model_description: A country's oil or gas supply routes, energy imports, power-grid projects, or dependency on external energy sources, and the strategic risk this creates.
energy_security.hypothesis: This text describes a country's energy supply routes or energy dependency risk.

maritime_security.model_description: Military naval activity at sea: warship patrols, freedom-of-navigation operations, naval exercises, or armed incidents and skirmishes involving military vessels.
maritime_security.hypothesis: This text describes military naval activity at sea.

maritime_dimensions.model_description: Non-military maritime and coastal economic activity: commercial port development, undersea cables, fisheries, or blue-economy projects, without an armed or military angle.
maritime_dimensions.hypothesis: This text describes commercial shipping, ports, or ocean economic activity without military conflict.

security_military_relations.description: Defence cooperation, arms deals, joint exercises
security_military_relations.model_description: Defence cooperation, arms sales, joint military exercises, training, or formal security pacts between two or more states' militaries.
security_military_relations.hypothesis: This text describes defence cooperation or arms sales between two countries' militaries.

border_issues.model_description: Territorial claims, boundary demarcation disputes, or land-border infrastructure and security issues between neighbouring states, not open combat.
border_issues.hypothesis: This text describes a territorial or land border dispute between two countries.

internal_conflict_china_role.description: Domestic conflict where China’s role is a factor
internal_conflict_china_role.model_description: China is explicitly named as playing a role in, supporting a side of, or influencing another country's internal political crisis or armed conflict.
internal_conflict_china_role.hypothesis: This text describes China's role in another country's internal conflict.

tech_digital_influence.description: Digital infrastructure, tech transfer, cyber influence
tech_digital_influence.model_description: Chinese-made technology, telecom equipment, 5G networks, surveillance systems, AI platforms, or digital-influence and propaganda operations exported to or used in another country.
tech_digital_influence.hypothesis: This text describes Chinese technology or digital influence being used in another country.

humanitarian_dimension.model_description: Refugee or displaced-persons flows, disaster relief, humanitarian aid delivery, or civilian suffering caused by conflict or a natural disaster.
humanitarian_dimension.hypothesis: This text describes refugees, disaster relief, or humanitarian suffering.

international_relations.model_description: Multilateral diplomacy, international organisations such as the UN, G7, or ASEAN, alliances, or global power competition among major powers, not specific to a China-bilateral relationship.
international_relations.hypothesis: This text describes multilateral diplomacy or global power competition.

b16_reduce_relations.description: Actions reducing the normal level of international interaction: breaking or downgrading diplomatic relations, halting aid, imposing embargoes or boycotts, ending negotiations, and expelling or withdrawing personnel.
b16_reduce_relations.model_description: Actions reducing the normal level of international interaction: breaking or downgrading diplomatic relations, halting aid, imposing embargoes or boycotts, ending negotiations, and expelling or withdrawing personnel.
b16_reduce_relations.hypothesis: This text describes one country cutting ties, expelling diplomats, or halting cooperation.
b16_reduce_relations.alertable_reason: Measured English-cue floor 1.2% of usable-text posts (~245 posts, ~5/day). Marginal against the baseline_mean >= 0.5/day support gate; coded for the record but excluded from daily alerting to avoid a mostly-empty panel.

b17_coerce.description: Actions to pressure or force a change in behaviour: seizing or damaging property, administrative sanctions, arrests, detentions and expulsions of individuals, and violation of territory.
b17_coerce.model_description: Actions to pressure or force a change in behaviour: seizing or damaging property, administrative sanctions, arrests, detentions and expulsions of individuals, and violation of territory.
b17_coerce.hypothesis: This text describes arrests, detentions, seizures, or a blockade.

b18_assault.description: Physical acts of violence, sabotage, or hijacking, and lethal or non-lethal attacks that do not amount to sustained fighting. Discrete attacks rather than continuous combat.
b18_assault.model_description: Physical acts of violence, sabotage, or hijacking, and lethal or non-lethal attacks that do not amount to sustained fighting. Discrete attacks rather than continuous combat.
b18_assault.hypothesis: This text describes an attack, bombing, or act of sabotage.

b19_fight.description: Open, extensive, continuous militarised conflict: conventional military force, blockades, occupation of territory, engagements with small or heavy weapons, violent repression, and cyberwarfare. Sustained combat rather than a single attack.
b19_fight.model_description: Open, extensive, continuous militarised conflict: conventional military force, blockades, occupation of territory, engagements with small or heavy weapons, violent repression, and cyberwarfare. Sustained combat rather than a single attack.
b19_fight.hypothesis: This text describes sustained armed fighting, shelling, or military occupation.

b20_mass_violence.description: Use of weapons of mass destruction, and mass expulsion, mass killing, ethnic cleansing, or genocide.
b20_mass_violence.model_description: Use of weapons of mass destruction, and mass expulsion, mass killing, ethnic cleansing, or genocide.
b20_mass_violence.hypothesis: This text describes mass killing, ethnic cleansing, genocide, or use of weapons of mass destruction.
b20_mass_violence.alertable_reason: Measured English-cue floor 0.3% of usable-text posts (~52 posts, ~1.1/day). Structurally cannot clear the baseline_mean >= 0.5/day support gate over this window, so it would produce a permanently empty alert panel. Still coded -- an atrocity claim belongs in the record even when it cannot be trend-alerted.
